/-!
# Erdős Problem 851

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/851](https://www.erdosproblems.com/851)
- [Pr26] D. Price and GPT-5.2 Pro, [Erdős problem 851](https://www.overleaf.com/read/svgbjzpxxppv#4eea7e) (2026)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos851

/--
`TwoPowAddSet r` is the set of integers of the form `2^k+n`, where `k ≥ 0` and `n` has at most `r`
prime divisors.
-/
def TwoPowAddSet (r : ℕ) := {(2 ^ k + n) | (k : ℕ) (n : ℕ) (_ : n.primeFactors.card ≤ r)}

/-- The set of integers of the form `2^k+p`, where `k ≥ 0` and `p` is prime. -/
def twoPowAddPrimeSet : Set ℕ := {(2 ^ k + p) | (k : ℕ) (p : ℕ) (_ : p.Prime)}

/--
The set of integers of the form `2^k+p` (where `p` is prime) has positive lower density.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_851.variants.romanoff : 0 < Set.lowerDensity twoPowAddPrimeSet := by
  sorry

/--
Let $\epsilon > 0$. Is there some $r \ll_\epsilon 1$ such that the density of integers of the
form $2^k+n$, where $k \geq 0$ and $n$ has at most $r$ prime divisors, is at least $1-\epsilon$?

This was proved affirmatively by Price and GPT-5.2 Pro [Pr26].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos851.lean#L37"]
theorem erdos_851 (ε : ℝ) (hε : ε ∈ Set.Ioo 0 1) : ∃ r,
    1 - ε ≤ (TwoPowAddSet r).lowerDensity := by
  sorry

end Erdos851

reformulations.difference: Lean restricts ε to (0,1) and permits the residual n = 0 in TwoPowAddSet. The distinct-prime-factor version stated in the remark following Theorem 1 of the cited paper uses every ε > 0 and requires n ≥ 1.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For ε ≥ 1 the requested lower bound is nonpositive, so nonnegativity of lower density supplies it immediately. Write A_r for the positive-residual version. For r ≥ 1, TwoPowAddSet r = insert 1 A_r: every added power 2^(k+1) already has the positive-residual representation 2^k + 2^k, whose residual has at most one distinct prime divisor. Inserting one element does not change lower density. Any existential budget r can be enlarged to max r 1 by monotonicity. Thus allowing zero does not change the existential density assertion. The combined equivalence was proved as Review851.main_reformulation in /workspace/review/equivalence.lean, without using either sorry-backed problem theorem; its axioms are only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound.

review.notes: Checked all four declarations, including quantifier scope, real-valued density, and small inputs. Lean computations confirm that primeFactors.card counts distinct primes and returns zero at 0 and 1. The cited paper explicitly states lower natural density and explicitly includes the distinct-prime-factor conclusion, so its stronger main theorem using multiplicity is not grounds for a finding. Both solved tags are supported by the available sources. The exact linked formal theorem and definitions match; a source dependency scan found no proof placeholders or custom axioms, but the external Lean 4.33.0 project was not rebuilt. Direct access to erdosproblems.com/851 and its forum was blocked by Cloudflare; the mathematical comparison used the cited primary paper, and current status was corroborated by the companion Erdős database. All experiments were confined to /workspace/review/.
